newsitem.title: USA: MFS Communications debt up on merger news.
newsitem.headline: MFS Communications debt up on merger news.

text.p: MFS Communications Co Inc's $1.6 billion in outstanding debt and preferred stock jumped roughly five points on news of a stock swap merger with WorldCom Inc.
MFS Communications' 8-7/8 percent senior discount notes due 2006 were last quoted at 68-3/4 bid, 69-1/8 offer. Dealers said the paper traded in the low 60's last week.
These notes traded at 65 at the beginning of 1996, according to Duff & Phelps fixed income research.
"We've seen a lot of quotes and it's traded up five. We think they could go a little higher," one dealer said.
WorldCom redeemed all of its outstanding rated debt on August 16, 1996.
Early on Monday, Standard & Poor's placed the single-B senior unsecured debt and B-minus preferred stock ratings of MFS Communications on CreditWatch with positive implications.
Moody's Investors Service Inc rates the notes B1 and has yet to comment on the affect of the merger.
S&P said MFS notes may be put to the company at 101 percent of accreted value in the event of a change of control. The WorldCom merger, as presently structured, would trigger this provision.
"MFS said that alternative transaction structures are being considered which might not allow holders the right to require MFS to repurchase the notes," S&P said.
MFS stock opened up more than 12 points at 47 compared to Friday's 34-7/8 close. Just before midday, it traded at 43.
Analysts said the merged entity will create a telecommunications giant with a market capitalization topping $23 billion.
It will combine the operations of the nation's number one, in terms of revenues, competitive local exchange company with those of the fourth-largest long distance carrier, S&P said.
S&P expects the combined entity will require external funding to support growth for at least the next three years, but synergies from the merger should offset any near-term financial weakness.
